hypotheses.premise: Who Leaves a Footprint? In a world where everyone films everything, the boss who first realises that attention is both power and danger survives; the loud one falls first, the quiet one wins mostly.
hypotheses.question: Which old way of ruling survives when every phone is a witness?
hypotheses.audience_reason: Crime-story and GTA fans get a four-way matchup with a character-select screen; casual viewers get one clear idea (attention is power and danger) that they recognise from their own feeds.
hypotheses.stakes: Each boss loses the thing his method depends on: Capone his publicity, Vito his control over people outside his circle, the invented Yakuza boss the street he cannot predict, Shelby his certainty that he is always ahead.
hypotheses.conflict: Each boss meets the same pressure (cameras, virality, money tech, chaos) and the elimination order is the story.
hypotheses.surprise: The one who falls first is the best-known and loudest (Capone), and in real history it was ledgers, not bullets, that did it; the winner is the quiet planner, and even he has a flaw.
hypotheses.payoff: The stat screen returns with changed stars and one debatable question: is winning quietly a victory or a different kind of loss?
uncertainties: Whether GTA VI itself shows civilians filming crimes is official only after a person watches trailer 1 (C-30); until then the line is worded 'appears to show' or 'GTA V-style'.
The year of the story is our assumption; Rockstar gives none (C-04).
Stats are the channel's own opinion, argued from history and canon, not facts.
counterarguments: A fan will say Vito would never retreat: answered by his own refusal of the heroin deal because his judges and politicians would turn (C-24).
A fan will say Shelby is violent: the script says so and uses it (C-28).
visual_opportunities: character-select screen with four portraits and star bars of our own layout
neon sunset causeway, phone-camera frames as picture-in-picture insets, ledger close-ups
invented comic Florida-style insets in a different, flatter drawing
audio_opportunities: a camera shutter and notification chirps as the pressure, a ledger page turn for the tax case
rights_risks: GTA VI names and unreleased features (RK-10)
actor likeness of Vito and Shelby (RK-07)

scores.why: Real-history spine (Capone's ledgers, Vito's refusal, Shelby's information) is sourced; the GTA VI side is labelled; the thesis gives every act one job.

hypotheses.premise: The Accountant Always Wins: in any era the boss with the best books and the quietest paperwork beats everyone, so the Yakuza boss wins and the film is a lesson in compliance.
hypotheses.question: Does the most boring boss always win?
hypotheses.audience_reason: A contrarian, money-focused take for viewers who like finance explainers.
hypotheses.stakes: Four methods are ranked by how well they survive an audit; the loser is whoever keeps the worst records.
hypotheses.surprise: Capone, the most famous gangster in history, was undone by exactly this: books.
hypotheses.payoff: The accountant wins, but the real Capone case shows the same tool also catches the accountants of crime.
uncertainties: Every real claim about Japanese organised crime in finance is unverified (C-42), so the Yakuza win would rest on our own invention.
GTA VI money systems are unknown; GTA V's exchanges are community-described (C-12).
counterarguments: It ignores Vito's and Shelby's strength, which is people and information, not books.
visual_opportunities: ledger pages, tax forms in neon, an auditor chasing a limousine

scores.why: Strong on Capone's ledgers, weak on the other three; the Yakuza claims are unverified and the story is a lecture.

hypotheses.premise: Nobody Beats Florida: whatever the method, chaos wins; all four bosses are eaten by absurdity, and the only survivor is the one who accepts he is a character in a Florida headline.
hypotheses.question: Can any boss out-plan a state that produces its own weather of nonsense?
hypotheses.audience_reason: Pure comedy for fans of absurd news-style humour and open-world chaos.
hypotheses.stakes: Each boss's plan is defeated by an invented absurd incident.
hypotheses.surprise: Capone's real retirement and death were in Florida (C-18), a quiet end for a loud man.
uncertainties: Almost no sourced claims: the comedy would be invented, which weakens the analysis requirement of RR-14.
Risk of reading as a retelling or sketch with no commentary on the game's systems.
counterarguments: It says nothing about GTA VI's systems, the weak case under RR-14.
rights_risks: invented incidents must stay fully invented (ER-15)

scores.why: Funny, but there is almost nothing to source and it fails the commentary-target test.

selected.why: Best balance of evidence and story (4 and 4); it is the creator's chosen thesis, it gives every act a job and a testable GTA system (phone cameras, social media, money), and H2/H3 score lower on evidence while not beating it on narrative. The Florida chaos of H3 survives as clearly invented comic inserts inside H1.

beats.what: Could a 1930s gangster survive a world where everyone has a camera? Four bosses drop into Vice City.
Character select: four bosses, five stats each, our rating, and the thesis in one line.
Who realises first that attention is both power and danger?
Capone: press fame as the 1930s version of going viral, then the ledger case. He falls first.
Vito: favours, judges, a legal oil import front, no heroin; his authority does not reach the people his network depends on.
Invented Florida-style chaos insert: no plan survives it.
The invented Yakuza boss wins the boardroom and loses the street.
Shelby: information, politics, ledgers, proxies, but overconfidence.
Stat screen returns with changed stars; who left a footprint; the debatable question left open.
